rubrics.criterion: The module that owns the per-connection activity ledger record (the module defining the record type, its evidence vocabulary, its hashed storage and its lookup/open API) now also implements the rules that interpret raw observations into ledger updates, so the accounting rules are decided by that module rather than assembled at consumer sites.
rubrics.rationale: This case exists because the defining module was shipped as a bare store while every consumer wrote its own copy of the interpretation rules; relocating rule ownership is the core semantic outcome the task asks for.

rubrics.criterion: Every site that previously maintained ledger state inline — in the TCP processing function, the UDP DNS processing function, both reset-attack classification legs, both evaluation-timeout verification branches, the insertion send path, the TTL probing path, and the two strategy implementations that fire treatments — now conveys its raw observation to the owning module instead of manipulating the record's fields where it stands.
rubrics.rationale: The maintenance concern spans the whole daemon, not only the sites that log; a repair limited to a subset of sites leaves the same drift problem in place, so coverage of the discovered scope is an independent obligation from the rule move itself.

rubrics.criterion: No function outside the owning module directly manipulates the ledger record's fields anymore; a consumer may obtain or open the record and pass it (or its key) to the owning module's API, but the interpretation of observations happens with the owner.
rubrics.rationale: Direct field manipulation at consumer sites is the mechanism by which the rules ended up outside their owner; its absence after repair is the observable, answerable form of the outcome.

rubrics.criterion: The cycle close-out is a single owning-module rule that derives the same verdict from the same evidence (reset evidence beats a response, which beats silence), applies the same conditional TTL-hint adjustments, marks the cycle verified, and produces the same summary line — rather than two mirrored consumer-side rule blocks.
rubrics.rationale: The timeout sweep contains the heaviest rule in the case, duplicated across two verification branches; consolidating it proves the rules were genuinely moved, not merely wrapped.

rubrics.criterion: The owning module's header exposes whatever new rule functions the repair introduced, so all consumer translation units (including the strategy implementations) compile against one declaration surface, and their implementation lives in the module that owns the record.
rubrics.rationale: In this C codebase the header is the boundary between the owner and the rest of the daemon; rule functions reachable from the pipeline and the strategies must be declared at that boundary to be a coherent relocation rather than hidden helpers.

rubrics.criterion: The strategy implementation files keep including the owning module's header and reference its API for their treatment journaling, i.e. their bookkeeping goes through the relocated rules rather than a private shortcut back into the record.
rubrics.rationale: The strategies self-report treatments outside the pipeline functions; keeping them on the owner's API is the associated change that makes the two strategy sites genuine participants instead of stragglers.

rubrics.criterion: The consumer sites that reconstruct the ledger key from a non-packet representation — the insertion send path building it from send-variable addresses and ports, and the probing path building it from probed port numbers — preserve the existing byte-order conversion when delegating, so they address the same record the pipeline paths do.
rubrics.rationale: These two sites are the case's key-conversion risk: their inputs are host-order while the ledger key follows the pipeline's convention; a relocation that drops the conversion silently splits one connection's cycle across two records.

rubrics.criterion: The inline bookkeeping blocks are gone from all consumer sites, including their local record pointers and the guard scaffolding that existed only to wrap the inline updates; no consumer keeps a leftover fragment or a commented-out copy of the old rule.
rubrics.rationale: Half-moved rules and dead scaffolding are the natural residue of this relocation and would keep the drift hazard alive even after the owner-side rules exist.

rubrics.criterion: No rule that interprets ledger observations remains duplicated in more than one place (e.g. an owning-module rule plus a retained inline copy of the same evidence/verdict/TTL logic at a consumer), so each accounting semantic has exactly one implementation.
rubrics.rationale: Duplicated rule logic was the stated maintenance pain; a repair that leaves both copies keeps the observed failure mode while still claiming the move.

rubrics.criterion: The pre-existing read-only consumer of the ledger (the reporting helper that prints a connection's ledger status for other incoming protocols) is not converted into a field-accessing consumer and keeps reporting through the owner's getter API.
rubrics.rationale: A uniform sweep can wrongly rebuild the one consumer that already followed the intended discipline; it must stay a getter-only caller, which is also what distinguishes reporting from rule maintenance in this case.

rubrics.criterion: No `[LEDGER]` log line changes level, format string, argument values, or emission condition: the cycle-closure summary, the strategy retry notice, and the junk-data retransmission notice must be produced exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: Operators parse these lines from deployed logs; the task's compatibility boundary calls them out, and the format strings encode the record's semantics (4-tuple, verdict, evidence bits, TTL hint).

rubrics.criterion: The repair introduces no crash and no dropped guard when the bounded ledger store refuses to create a record (or when a key has none): every delegation is safe without a record, paths that previously skipped their update still perform no update in that situation, and the store's full warning behavior is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: Every injected site was conditional on the record existing; consolidation is exactly where a NULL dereference or an unconditional write is most likely to appear.

rubrics.criterion: TTL-hint semantics are preserved: the server-side initial TTL is adopted only when no hint exists yet on the first response, a confirmed probing value replaces the hint only when unset or smaller, the reset-evidence increment stays bounded at 255, and the no-response decrement still applies only above 3.
rubrics.rationale: The hint drives the TTL of crafted packets, so these four bounds and conditions are the case's most behavior-sensitive rules; each one is cheap to break during relocation and none is covered by the build alone.

rubrics.criterion: The junk-data retransmission notice still fires only for connections whose response evidence was already set at the time the treatment was re-sent (the response check is not reordered after the injection mark or inverted), and the strategy retry notice still appears from the third dispatched strategy onward.
rubrics.rationale: Two sites read the record's state to decide further updates; ordering and threshold details are the failure modes that survive a clean build and only show up as wrong log output.
